analyst_view.overall: Juventus (7th, 18 points, LWLWD) host 19th-placed Venezia in Sunday's lunchtime game and need a win after dropping points to lower-table sides. Spalletti is expected to use a back three (Gatti, Bremer, Lucumi) with McKennie and Cabal wide because Cambiaso and Celik are still doubtful; Kalulu, Locatelli, Khephren Thuram, Grabara and Nico Gonzalez are out (mostly counted), Yildiz is back training with the ball but not ready, and Conceicao and Zhegrova are available again. Venezia under Davide Nicola play a compact 3-5-2 built for counters through Yeboah and Akor Adams; Franjic is out, while Adorante (counted out by the numbers) is back in group training but short of rhythm. Referee Alberto Arena has a low card record on only three games, which the numbers already blend in.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Juve are short of their usual wide players and Venezia will sit in a dense midfield, which offsets Juve's need to win and the return of Conceicao as an option; Adorante's return for Venezia is from the bench at best, so I stay at about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, already raised for Juve's recent corner count (+12%). Venezia defending deep should give Juve plenty of corners, but that is what the numbers already show, so I stay at about 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards, cut for both teams' quiet recent run (about -10% and -13%) and for Arena's low record on just three games. Nicola's sides defend aggressively and Venezia are fighting relegation, which a three-game referee sample can't capture; a mild lean up to about 2.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.4 shots, already lifted for Venezia's recent shooting (+18%). Juve will have the ball against a compact block with Kolo Muani, Woltemade and Alajbegovic expected up front, close to what the numbers expect, so I stay at about 30.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Juve's expected front three is their usual one and their recent accuracy is already counted, so I stay at about 8.9.
